newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTZ-CRA puts sold sign on zinc mine.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA puts sold sign on zinc mine.

text.p: Global miner RTZ-CRA said on Wednesday the settlement of indigenous land-title claims to the Century zinc project in northern Australia paved the way for the sale of the discovery to Pasminco Ltd.
Zinc producer Pasminco agreed in January to buy the Century zinc project and nearby Dugald River zinc projects from RTZ-CRA for A$345 million, subject to settlement of the land claims.
The claims were settled on Wednesday morning when the Queensland state government consented to a deal struck between 12 Aborigines and the project company, Century Zinc Ltd (CZL).
"This advance opens the way for the sale of CZL to Pasminco Ltd and the subsequent development of the mine project...," RTZ-CRA said in a statement.
Pasminco bought the mine because it needs Century's low-iron zinc concentrates to feed its Budel smelter in the Netherlands.
Pasminco has said the low-iron concentrates would ensure the smelter complied with a requirement that it cease generating hazardous zinc residue called jarosite.
Remaining issues to be settled before Century changes hands are the mining lease, lease for port facilities in the Gulf of Carpentaria and a licence for the pipeline from mine to port.
These are expected to take several months to finalise, RTZ-CRA said.
